excerpts.text: A route is an ordered list of stops. A label names one stop. A tag groups stops by a shared feature. Changing a label does not change the route order. Rearranging stops changes the route order. Two stops may share a tag while retaining different labels.

entries.title: Routes, labels and tags
entries.scope: Invented structural fixture. No real course materials or student trial were processed.

blocks.text: Plan in two steps: choose different labels for the two stops; then choose a feature both stops share and use it as their tag. Keep the proposed order explicit when you later write the route. The shared tag groups the stops without collapsing their different labels.
The final route description is outside the requested help stage.
blocks.nextStep: Write your own route description after choosing its labels and shared tag.

requirements.text: Plan a route with two differently labeled stops that share one tag.
requirements.basis: Task text establishes the requirement; the plan explains how to choose distinct labels and a shared tag. This assesses planning support, not student completion.
The explicit student request limits help to planning, leaving the final description to the student.
requirements.nextStep: Write the description yourself, or explicitly request a later support stage.
